The core operator is the bounded abstention threshold γ_δ which partitions input space into prediction and abstention regions based on posterior probability deviation from 1/2. This induces a dual structure: predictions occur outside the ambiguity band, while abstentions happen inside it. The boundary rule introduces randomness to maintain fairness when the cumulative distribution function exhibits jumps, ensuring that even at decision boundaries, abstention does not introduce systematic bias. The histogram estimator provides a computationally efficient way to approximate the true posterior η(x), splitting estimation error into stochastic and deterministic components. These primitives together form a robust framework for binary classification under bounded abstention, suitable for real-time applications such as GSE’s weekly board volume control. Failure modes include overfitting due to insufficient data in sparse regions, or misalignment between estimated and true thresholds when the underlying distribution deviates from assumed smoothness properties.
